client.name: Chanel S.A.S.
client.subtitle: Luxury Goods | Fashion, Fragrance & Beauty
client.description: Chanel is a French luxury fashion house known for haute couture, ready-to-wear fashion, fragrances, cosmetics, and fine jewellery. Founded by Gabrielle 'Coco' Chanel, it operates over 500 boutiques in more than 100 countries. It serves high-net-worth clients worldwide and remains one of the most valuable privately owned luxury brands in the world.

serviceAreas.title: Fashion & Accessories
serviceAreas.desc: Designs and sells haute couture, ready-to-wear clothing, handbags, shoes, and accessories worldwide.

serviceAreas.title: Fragrance & Beauty
serviceAreas.desc: Produces iconic perfumes like Chanel No. 5 and a full range of cosmetics and skincare.

serviceAreas.title: Watches & Fine Jewellery
serviceAreas.desc: Creates and sells high-end timepieces and jewellery collections through boutiques and select partners.

serviceAreas.title: Digital & Client Experience
serviceAreas.desc: Manages e-commerce, digital content, and personalised client engagement across online channels.

serviceAreas.title: Corporate & Operations
serviceAreas.desc: Runs finance, legal, HR, IT, and supply chain functions supporting all global business units.

locations.label: Headquarters
locations.address: 135 Avenue Charles de Gaulle, Neuilly-sur-Seine, France

priorities.title: Go Digital Without Losing Brand Exclusivity
priorities.desc: Chanel is digitising its operations and client experience while keeping the sense of exclusivity that defines the brand. This means using technology to serve clients better, not to mass-market products. Teams need tools that help them work faster while keeping all communications polished and on-brand.
priorities.pains: Inconsistent brand voice across digital channels; slow approval cycles for content; difficulty maintaining tone guidelines across a large global team

priorities.title: Deliver a Seamless Omnichannel Client Experience
priorities.desc: Clients expect a consistent experience whether they visit a boutique, browse online, or speak to an advisor. Chanel is aligning its in-store, digital, and service teams to deliver that. This needs better information sharing and faster responses to client needs across all regions.
priorities.pains: Siloed client data across systems; slow handoffs between in-store and online teams; difficulty tracking client preferences and history in real time

priorities.title: Build Sustainable and Responsible Luxury Practices
priorities.desc: Chanel has committed to reducing its environmental footprint and sourcing materials responsibly. This affects suppliers, manufacturing, packaging, and how the company reports progress publicly. Teams across operations, finance, and communications all play a role in tracking and sharing sustainability goals.
priorities.roles: Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, Communications, HR
priorities.pains: Consolidating sustainability data from multiple sources is manual; ESG reporting relies on spreadsheets; coordinating sustainability messaging across markets is inconsistent

priorities.title: Attract, Develop, and Keep Top Talent
priorities.desc: As a premium employer, Chanel competes for skilled professionals in fashion, technology, finance, and client services. It invests heavily in learning and development to keep staff skilled and engaged. Sharing knowledge and helping employees grow within the business is a key focus.
priorities.roles: HR, Learning & Development, Managers, Department Heads
priorities.pains: Inconsistent onboarding across markets; difficulty tracking training progress globally; institutional knowledge is lost when experienced staff leave

priorities.title: Use Data to Make Faster Business Decisions
priorities.desc: Chanel is moving toward more data-driven decision making, from sales forecasting to inventory planning to client segmentation. Leaders need clear, timely information to act quickly. This requires better tools for analysing data, summarising findings, and sharing insights with the right people fast.
priorities.roles: Finance, Strategy, Operations, Managers, Regional Directors
priorities.pains: Data is trapped in disconnected systems; manual reporting is slow; turning raw data into clear recommendations for leadership takes too long

capabilities.objectives: Office staff handle the day-to-day communications, documents, and coordination that keep Chanel running across all functions. They support creative, commercial, and corporate teams across global markets. Their work needs to be accurate, well-presented, and aligned with Chanel's brand standards. Getting the details right is as important here as it is on the runway.
capabilities.painPoints: Writing polished emails and documents takes time, especially when handling multiple requests at once. Finding the right version of a file across SharePoint, OneDrive, and email is often frustrating. Meeting notes are rarely captured or followed up on. Reformatting documents to match brand templates is repetitive work that happens every day.
capabilities.keyActivities: drafting internal briefing notes and memos, formatting brand-aligned presentations in PowerPoint, managing shared inboxes in Outlook, coordinating cross-team meeting schedules, updating project trackers in Excel, filing documents to shared SharePoint drives

capabilities.objectives: Managers at Chanel lead teams across retail, operations, creative, and corporate functions. They translate company strategy into clear priorities and remove blockers so work moves forward. They also report upward to regional directors and global leadership on performance and progress. Keeping distributed teams aligned and informed takes up much of their time.
capabilities.painPoints: Preparing weekly status updates and performance summaries takes too long. Running effective team meetings in Teams is difficult when agendas are not set in advance. Tracking tasks and decisions across email threads means things fall through the cracks. Getting consistent information out to teams spread across different time zones is a regular challenge.
capabilities.keyActivities: running weekly team briefings in Teams, reviewing and approving staff reports and proposals, tracking project milestones in shared Excel files, preparing performance update slides for regional leadership, cascading strategy updates to direct reports, reviewing team workloads and reassigning tasks

capabilities.objectives: The finance and operations team manages budgets, forecasts, procurement, and financial reporting across all Chanel markets. They work closely with regional leads and global HQ to make sure costs are controlled and resources are used well. Accuracy and timeliness are critical, as leadership relies on their numbers to make major decisions.
capabilities.painPoints: Consolidating financial data from multiple regional systems into a single Excel model is slow and error-prone. Writing narrative commentary for board reports takes significant effort every month. Version control on large Excel files breaks down when multiple people edit them at the same time. Chasing down purchase order approvals over email causes unnecessary delays.
capabilities.keyActivities: consolidating monthly P&L reports across business units, preparing budget versus actual variance analysis in Excel, drafting finance commentary for leadership reports, processing and tracking purchase orders, coordinating with suppliers on invoicing and payments, preparing slides for quarterly business reviews

capabilities.objectives: The HR team manages recruitment, onboarding, learning, employee relations, and performance across Chanel's global workforce. They help attract talent that fits Chanel's culture and high standards. They design and deliver learning programmes to develop staff at every level. Handling sensitive people data carefully and consistently is central to the role.
capabilities.painPoints: Creating onboarding documents and training materials in Word and PowerPoint takes time and often goes out of date quickly. Tracking learning completions and performance review cycles in Excel is fragile and hard to scale globally. Communicating HR policy updates to all staff consistently across markets is a repeated challenge. Writing job descriptions and interview guides for each new role is largely repetitive work.
capabilities.keyActivities: drafting job descriptions and offer letters in Word, preparing onboarding packs for new joiners, coordinating performance review schedules, creating training presentation decks in PowerPoint, tracking headcount and attrition data in Excel, communicating policy updates via Outlook to regional HR leads

capabilities.objectives: Sales and client service teams work directly with Chanel's clients in boutiques and through digital channels. They are responsible for delivering the brand's signature client experience and building lasting relationships. They handle inquiries, after-sales service, and VIP client management. Every interaction is expected to reflect the Chanel brand perfectly.
capabilities.painPoints: Finding up-to-date product information and client communication templates quickly during a live client interaction is difficult. Writing personalised follow-up messages to high-value clients takes time to get right. Logging client interactions and preferences across systems is inconsistent across teams. Coordinating with other boutiques or HQ to resolve client issues involves long, slow email threads.
capabilities.keyActivities: responding to client inquiries via Outlook, preparing personalised client outreach and follow-up messages, logging client feedback and interaction notes, coordinating stock availability checks with warehouse teams, preparing boutique performance reports in Excel, drafting client event invitations and briefings

capabilities.objectives: The IT team manages Chanel's global technology infrastructure, including Microsoft 365, retail systems, and internal applications. They support all staff with tools, access, and troubleshooting across a wide range of devices and markets. They also manage security, compliance, and data governance across the organisation. Keeping systems running reliably is critical to business continuity.
capabilities.painPoints: Writing and maintaining IT process documentation in Word is inconsistent and often left incomplete. Managing Microsoft 365 user requests and access permissions at scale is time-consuming work. Communicating system outages and maintenance windows clearly to all staff is harder than it should be. Writing technical guides that non-technical staff can actually understand takes significant effort each time.
capabilities.keyActivities: managing Microsoft 365 user accounts and licence provisioning, writing and updating IT documentation and runbooks in Word, responding to helpdesk requests via Teams and Outlook, communicating system maintenance windows to the business, reviewing IT security alerts and incident logs, coordinating software rollout communications across departments

workflows.name: New Collection Launch Communications

steps.d: Marketing manager shares the collection brief with creative and communications leads via Teams.
Communications team writes press release and talking points in Word for internal review.
Brand and legal teams review and comment on documents before final sign-off.
Regional teams adapt approved messages for local markets and translate where needed.
Final content is shared via Teams channels and Outlook to retail and PR teams.

workflows.friction: Approval rounds take too long because feedback arrives through separate email threads rather than one shared document. Regional adaptations often lag behind the launch date.

workflows.name: Monthly Business Performance Review

steps.d: Finance team exports figures from retail and ERP systems into Excel for analysis.
Analyst compiles key metrics and writes commentary in PowerPoint and Word.
Regional managers check numbers and add context before the leadership meeting.
Director presents the summary in a Teams call with senior leaders.
Meeting notes and agreed actions are emailed to attendees after the call.

workflows.friction: Combining data from different regional sources manually is slow and causes last-minute errors. Meeting actions are not always captured and often get lost between sessions.

workflows.name: New Employee Onboarding

steps.d: HR sends the new joiner a welcome email and onboarding documents via Outlook.
IT provisions Microsoft 365 accounts and business system access for the new employee.
HR hosts an onboarding session on Teams and shares a SharePoint induction guide.
New joiner works through mandatory compliance and brand training modules.
Line manager holds a 30-day review meeting via Teams to discuss progress.

workflows.friction: Onboarding materials are spread across different folders and often out of date. New joiners are unsure where to find key information and rely on colleagues to fill the gaps.

workflows.name: VIP Client Event Planning

steps.d: Client relations team reviews VIC records and agrees on the invite list.
Communications team writes personalised event invitations in Word using approved brand templates.
Operations team manages venue, catering, and scheduling using Outlook calendar and Teams.
Invitations go out via Outlook and responses are tracked manually in an Excel sheet.
Client advisors send personalised thank-you messages and log notes from the event.

workflows.friction: Coordinating boutique, logistics, and communications teams creates too many overlapping email chains. RSVP tracking in Excel is manual and hard to share in real time across teams.

glossary.d: The French word for 'house', used to describe Chanel as a brand institution with its own history and values. Staff often say 'the Maison' to mean Chanel itself.
A Chanel retail store, typically in a premium shopping district. Each boutique is designed to deliver a consistent luxury client experience.
A sales associate who works directly with clients in boutiques or through digital channels. They manage the full client relationship, not just a single transaction.
Chanel's shared services function covering finance, HR, IT, and compliance across multiple regions. It exists to support efficiency and consistency across markets.
A senior leader responsible for Chanel's performance across a defined geography such as Asia Pacific or Europe. They report directly to global leadership.
Short for Environmental, Social, and Governance. Chanel uses ESG reporting to show progress on sustainability commitments and responsible business practices.
Key Performance Indicator. Teams use KPIs to measure progress against sales targets, client satisfaction scores, and operational goals.
The top executive group at Chanel, including the CEO and divisional presidents. They set overall strategy and priorities for the business.
Short for Very Important Client. These are Chanel's top-tier clients who receive priority access to new collections, private events, and personalised service.
The business unit responsible for Chanel's perfumes and cosmetics lines. It operates separately from fashion but follows the same brand guidelines.
The unit that designs, makes, and sells Chanel's timepieces and jewellery collections. It operates through dedicated boutiques and select retail partners.
The team managing Chanel's e-commerce site, digital marketing, and online client journey. They work closely with retail and communications teams.
An in-boutique event where a curated selection of new pieces is shown to select clients before general availability. Often used to engage VIC clients.
Custom-made, high-end fashion produced in small quantities using hand craftsmanship. Chanel's couture collections are shown twice a year in Paris.
Also called prêt-à-porter, these are Chanel's off-the-rack seasonal fashion lines sold in boutiques worldwide. They are distinct from the custom couture collections.
A specialised workshop where Chanel's craftspeople produce garments and accessories. The ateliers are at the heart of the couture production process.
Chanel's annual collection celebrating the traditional artisan skills of its partner ateliers. It is held each December in a different global location.
A seasonal range of clothing and accessories presented at a runway show. Chanel produces multiple collections per year, including Spring/Summer and Autumn/Winter.
A live presentation where Chanel shows its latest collection to buyers, press, and VIP clients. These shows set the direction for seasonal sales and media coverage.
The French term for ready-to-wear fashion. At Chanel, this refers to the seasonal clothing lines sold through boutiques and online.
A person, typically a public figure, who represents Chanel in public-facing campaigns. They embody the brand's values and image to a wider audience.
An AI assistant built into Microsoft 365 apps like Teams, Outlook, and Word. It helps staff write, summarise, and work through information faster.
Microsoft's intranet and document storage platform used by Chanel teams to share files and internal resources. It is the central hub for company documentation.
A Microsoft tool for building visual reports and dashboards from data. Used by Chanel's finance and operations teams to track business performance.
Chanel's core ERP system used to manage financial transactions, procurement, and supply chain processes. It is the source of truth for operational and financial data.
Customer relationship management software used to track client interactions and purchase history. Client advisors use it to manage VIC relationships.
Chanel's HR platform used for managing employee records, payroll, recruitment, and performance reviews. It is the main people system for HR teams globally.
The process of bringing a new employee into Chanel, covering access setup, training, and cultural orientation. It typically spans the first 30 to 90 days.
The function responsible for designing and delivering training programmes for Chanel staff. It covers product knowledge, technical skills, and leadership development.
A formal process where employees and managers discuss goals, achievements, and development areas. Chanel conducts these on an annual or semi-annual basis.
Human Resource Information System. The platform, currently Workday, that holds all employee data and supports HR processes across Chanel globally.
The recruitment function within HR responsible for attracting and hiring staff across all levels and markets. It manages job postings, interviews, and offers.
The internal rules that define how Chanel's name, logo, tone, and visual identity should be used. All teams are expected to follow these in every piece of communications.
